hypothesis: The resolved v14 HYPE lifecycle can distinguish entry-quality, exit, and L2 hypotheses without changing the live strategy after one outcome. The next portfolio generation should remove historically rejected generic cross-asset breakout transfers, while every proposed HYPE exit or model change remains report-only until independent profile-matched evidence supports it.
decision: Preserve the resolved v14 HYPE lifecycle and keep the currently authorized runtime unchanged; all four venue assets are flat and no owned order remains. Reject the exact completed-five-minute RSI14/EMA7 reversal exit because it materially worsened net return and drawdown in both chronological blocks. Keep the HYPE L2 Ridge model annotation-only because both resolved predictions lost and directional sign agreement is zero. Keep every support-decay profit-lock policy report-only: all three would have reduced this HYPE loss by an estimated $0.2824, but the eleven-lifecycle mixed-profile mechanism still reduces mean normalized return versus actual exits. Reject relaxing 5m_not_breakout because the frozen HYPE and SOL aligned-book challengers remain negative, short-only, and below profit factor one. Evidence-routed v18 remains an inactive next-flat research candidate requiring explicit operator approval and a fresh verified backup before activation; this revision does not place, close, gate, resize, restart, or promote anything.
falsifier: Revisit the exit rejection only if independent profile-matched long and short lifecycles under an unchanged predeclared rule improve after actual fees, funding, and stop precedence without truncating larger winners. Revisit the L2 rejection only if later unchanged-bundle outcomes show stable positive after-friction score-band discrimination. Revisit the entry relaxation only if later non-overlapping long and short paths under the frozen contract produce stable profit factor above one without single-path concentration. The v18 candidate is invalidated by route overlap, execution outside Hulk|BTC, ETH-pullback|ETH, and HYPE-breakout|HYPE, sizing or protection drift, or activation without explicit authority and a verified flat backup.
limitations: The v14 run contains two closed shorts and no completed long, so it cannot establish bidirectional edge or portfolio repeatability.
The resolved HYPE lifecycle is one profile-matched observation; its favorable profit-lock counterfactual cannot establish an exit policy.
The support-decay mechanism was originally identified post hoc and pools normalized lifecycles across five source profiles; it is mechanism evidence rather than current-profile portfolio PnL.
The L2 Ridge observer contains only two resolved shorts and cannot estimate long-side behavior, calibration, or stable score discrimination.
The one-blocker challengers use recorded BBO capacity and simulated exits rather than proof of private IOC fills; both samples remain short-only.
The v18 candidate removes historically weak transfers but is not a proven profitable portfolio; ETH has no forward fills and HYPE's exact execution history remains negative.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, sizing policy, backend process, checkpoint process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
